newsitem.title: USA: No survivors in plane collision at Illinois airport.
newsitem.headline: No survivors in plane collision at Illinois airport.

text.p: Two planes collided on the ground and burst into flames at the local airport at Quincy, Illinois, and all on board were killed, police said on Tuesday.
"I'm confirming there are no survivors," Quincy Deputy Police Chief John LaTour told CNN. "What I can't confirm are the number of fatalities."
A police spokeswoman told Reuters that a United Air commuter plane flight arriving from Chicago, after stopping at Burlington, Iowa, crashed with a small plane at the municipal airport.
Police said unofficially they believed there were nine passengers and two crew on the United flight and two people in private plane on the ground.
The crash occurred at 6:02 p.m. EST (2300 GMT).
Quincy is located on the Mississippi River, 105 miles (170 km) north of St. Louis and 210 miles (340 km) south west of Chicago.
